chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Isma'il ibn Abi Bakr al-Hadrami narrated to me from Ali, Abu al-Akrad, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I accept work in which there is goldsmithing and engraving, so I make a condition with the engraver for a certain amount between me and him: ten units for five dirhams, or twenty for ten. When the calculation is complete, I say to him, 'Do well,' and I deduct it from the condition I made with him. He (the Imam) said, 'With his good will.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'There is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a craftsman to deduct a tip from the agreed contract price?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of 'ihsan' (voluntary bonus) in labor contracts, distinguishing it from a fixed wage deduction by emphasizing that the worker must explicitly consent to the deduction from the principal sum. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that contractual flexibility is permissible as long as the worker’s satisfaction ('bitayyif nafsih') is secured, preventing any sense of coercion in the final settlement.
